accuracy.evidence: Matches DfE Development Matters 3 and 4 year olds, PSED ('Be increasingly independent in meeting their own care needs, e.g. brushing teeth, using the toilet, washing and drying their hands thoroughly'), and the Harvard Center on the Developing Child description of working memory as an executive function that holds a plan in mind. The handwashing order (wet, soap, rub, rinse, dry) follows NHS and CDC handwashing guidance; now and next boards and visual timetables are standard early years practice.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real errors at this age: believing order never matters (socks after shoes, drying before rinsing), skipping a step such as soap, relying on an adult for every step, and mistaking a later step for the next one. They appear in the prediction 'Can shoes go on before socks? Yes, any order', in the lab feedback (That comes later, That step is done already) and in twelve challenge messages.

lab_distinct.evidence: Mechanics are about routines themselves: a Now and Next board that shifts forward after each step, numbered routine boxes that reject a card with the reason it must come first, a bedtime strip with a gap to fill, a two-day snack routine where the picture reminders are removed on day 5 (fading prompts), and a swapped pair in Pip's plan that the child finds and swaps back. It passed the 30% shingle gate against flagtwo and every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child first uses the now and next frame, then discovers that some steps have to come before others, then reasons from before and after to find a missing step, then repeats a routine from memory once the pictures go, and finally checks someone else's plan. Each confirm message states the idea only after the child has done it.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Can shoes go on before socks? Yes, any order' (the boxes reject shoes in box 1 with the reason) and 'Doing a routine every day makes it... harder to remember' (day 5 is done with no pictures at all).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with thirteen distinct m= wrong-answer messages: socks already on, bed is for night, dry is not yet, snack comes after clean hands, shoes are not bedtime, breakfast is morning, something did go wrong, the door is last, once is not enough, skipping makes it harder, washing comes first, and sitting comes before eating.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short read-aloud sentences and the routine words first, next, then, last; adult text stays within the family limit while naming routine, sequence, working memory, executive function, now and next board and visual timetable. Every card pairs one emoji with one or two words, and the young class keeps tap targets large.

no_filler.evidence: Passes the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate. Kid paragraphs each do one job (what a routine is, what comes next, order matters, practice); adult paragraphs cover the skill and curriculum, the tools and fading, the mistakes, and what the lab does; the family tip is a concrete photo strip by the sink.

mobile.evidence: Walkthrough passes on iPhone 13 (390 px). Phone screenshots of every step were checked: strips of four and five cards fit the width, card words are readable, the now and next board stays inside the canvas, and every card has a matching full-width button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin (one button per card choice, Box 1 to 4 after picking, one button per card in Pip's plan). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the whole state, for example 'Now: Soap. Choices: Rub, Dry, Rinse' or the routine with the gap. axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes.

sources: DfE (2023) Development Matters: Personal, Social and Emotional Development, 3 and 4 year olds
Harvard Center on the Developing Child: Executive Function and Self-Regulation (working memory)
NHS: How to wash your hands; CDC: Handwashing steps (wet, lather, scrub, rinse, dry)
Early years visual support guidance: now and next boards and visual timetables (e.g. NHS and local authority SEND guidance)
